extracted.intended_audience: policy advocates, administrative lawyers, agency staff, and stakeholders interested in federal rulemaking and deregulatory strategies
extracted.subtask_description: A step‑by‑step guide explaining the procedures agencies must follow under the Administrative Procedure Act to promulgate, alter, or repeal regulations, plus statutory exemptions and political control mechanisms that affect rulemaking and rollbacks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is the Agency Following the APA?
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the Agency Following the APA?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Administrative Procedure Act (APA) governs how agencies conduct rulemakings and recissions. The paper explains the specific steps agencies must take to promulgate, alter, or repeal regulations, and the exemptions provided in statute that agencies can use in certain circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency Rulemaking Authority
rubrics_metrics.description: When Congress passes legislation, it often explicitly authorizes federal agencies to implement provisions of the law through rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although agency rulemaking authority comes from Congress, understanding whether a particular rule or rollback is lawful requires tracing the statutory delegation of authority from Congress to the agency and whether the agency is acting within that delegation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Priorities and Directives
rubrics_metrics.description: While agency rulemaking authority comes from Congress, the president sets priorities for agencies, often through Executive Orders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An incoming administration uses executive directives to set which rulemakings to pursue and which existing rules to target for rescission or replacement; these political directives shape agency agendas and can prompt extensive rulemaking activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Targeting Existing Rules for Rescission or Replacement
rubrics_metrics.description: An incoming administration decides which existing federal rules to target with recission or replacement and directs agencies on what new rulemakings to undertake.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This criterion captures the selection and prioritization process by which agencies (at the direction of the Administration) identify rules to unwind or revise, including strategic choices about sequencing, scope, and legal theories for rescission or replacement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Undermining Agency Expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: The actions taken by the administration: (1) undermined agency expertise,
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as a characteristic of past deregulatory efforts; evaluating rollbacks should include whether actions rely on or cause erosion of agency technical or scientific expertise (an indicator of problematic process or substitution of policy judgments for expert determinations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Restricting Public Participation in Agency Action
rubrics_metrics.description: The actions taken by the administration: (2) restricted public participation in agency action,
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This identifies reductions or procedural shortcuts in notice-and-comment or other participatory mechanisms as a criterion for assessing the legitimacy or legality of a rulemaking or rollback; restricting participation is an anti-pattern flagged by the paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimizing Regulation-Triggering Events
rubrics_metrics.description: The actions taken by the administration: (3) took actions that minimized regulation-triggering events,
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy or administrative steps that avoid events or conditions that would otherwise trigger regulatory obligations are cited as a tactic; assessing rollbacks includes checking for manipulations that prevent regulatory triggers rather than addressing underlying policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-interpreting Statutes to Limit Agencies’ Authority to Regulate
rubrics_metrics.description: The actions taken by the administration: (4) re-interpreted statutes in novel ways to limit agencies’ authority to regulate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Novel or aggressive statutory interpretations used to shrink perceived agency authority are a key factor in deregulatory strategies; evaluating a rollback includes examining the statutory interpretation relied upon and its fit with precedent and statutory text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory Exemptions Agencies Can Use
rubrics_metrics.description: the exemptions provided in statute that agencies can use in certain circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guide discusses statutory exemptions to ordinary APA procedures that agencies may invoke in limited circumstances; assessing a rulemaking or rollback requires identifying any claimed exemptions and whether their use is justified under the statute and case law.
